correctness.rationale: The 24 signed coordinate-permutation vertices form the regular rhombicuboctahedron; its 48 edges fall into 24 small-sign-flip edges and 24 large-coordinate-swap edges. The section side count equals edges with endpoints on opposite sides of the plane. Exhaustive exact clipping of all 16 four-line patterns in the 1/48 spherical normal sector leaves exactly six positive-area sign chambers: one with eight sides and five with twelve, with all vertex-linear-form signs certified constant throughout each chamber in Q(sqrt(2)). The octagonal condition is x>(1+sqrt(2))y+z. Spherical Girard evaluation of its triangular normal cone gives angles pi/4,theta,theta and area 2theta-3pi/4, proving the complete Haar law. The checker executed successfully from the actual package path, and independent random normals corroborate but do not establish the universal result.

value.rationale: The small rhombicuboctahedron is a canonical Archimedean solid. A complete two-outcome distribution is mathematically motivated because central-section combinatorial complexity is a fundamental slicing invariant; the absence of ten-sided sections despite 48 edges is a structural forbidden-type result. The sharp inequality in sorted normal coordinates identifies the event geometrically, and its elementary exact Haar probability supplies a reusable benchmark rather than an arbitrary finite table or routine perturbation.
